turns.question: Should height and width be the same, and how well is the reliability of unequal dimensions established?

answers.text:
Inference from code: The native file does not need to have this height: scipy.ndimage.zoom resamples spatial axes with order=1 to the configured (height, width), retaining the original time count. The code does not force height and width to be equal. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L120-L120) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_stimulus.py#L102-L111)

Inference from code: There is no explicit width==height validator, but the current signal code assigns stimulus.data_shape() to stim_width,stim_height,stim_frames, whereas resampling constructs (height,width,T). It then passes these reversed dimension names to a kernel that indexes y by rows and x by columns. Unequal dimensions can therefore misindex coordinates; this revision does not establish reliable rectangular-stimulus support. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L120-L120) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/signal_synthesizer.py#L149-L152) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/signal_synthesizer.py#L201-L210) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/kernels/gaussian_kernel.cu#L49-L60)

turns.question: How does device numbering in default_gpu relate to CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES?

answers.text: Inference from code: Setup overwrites CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES with default_gpu followed by the sorted unique additional IDs. answers.text: Inference from code: Default sigmas are generated with linspace(min_sigma,max_sigma,num_sigmas), including endpoints, and used as the Gaussian model's third parameter. The kernel divides squared coordinate distance by 2*sigma²; sigmas share the degree units of the coordinate grid. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L145-L150) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L136-L150) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/kernels/gaussian_kernel.cu#L33-L60) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_stimulus.py#L39-L40)

For n>1 and finite arithmetic, the ideal signed step is (max_sigma − min_sigma)/(n − 1): min_sigma supplies the start, max_sigma the stop, and num_sigmas the count. turns.question: How does raising or lowering peak_disp change the HRF shape? Separately, how does raising or lowering under_disp change it?

answers.text:
Inference from code: Increasing positive peak_disp at fixed peak_delay decreases the positive gamma shape parameter peak_delay/peak_disp and increases its scale. Both enter gamma.pdf, so this changes the sampled positive-component shape; an exact final HRF width or fitting benefit is not established. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/hrf_generator.py#L47-L56)

Inference from code: Decreasing positive peak_disp at fixed peak_delay increases the positive gamma shape parameter and reduces its scale. Both enter gamma.pdf and alter sampled component shape; values at or below zero raise ValueError. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/hrf_generator.py#L47-L56)

Inference from code: Increasing positive under_disp at fixed under_shoot_delay decreases the undershoot gamma shape parameter under_delay/under_disp and increases its scale. Both enter gamma.pdf, changing the sampled component that is subtracted from the peak. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/hrf_generator.py#L47-L61)

turns.question: Does stimulus.directory need to identify a file or a directory? Separately, what contents should stimulus_filepath point to?

answers.text: Code: In BIDS mode, stimulus/directory is a folder listed for files ending exactly in .nii.gz. The task label from each measured filename is matched to the task entity in stimulus filenames; the first match is selected. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L199-L200) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L154-L164) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L175-L178) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L35-L41)

Code: The actual XML location is input_datasrc/fixed_paths/stimulus_filepath. Non-BIDS mode checks that this is a file, extracts task-<label> from its basename, and loads it as the single stimulus used for the measured-file loop. Code: If the fixed stimulus is not a file, discovery logs the specified path and exits with status 1. turns.question: Does stimulus.directory need to identify a file or a directory? Separately, what contents should stimulus_filepath point to?

answers.text: Code: In BIDS mode, stimulus/directory is a folder listed for files ending exactly in .nii.gz. The task label from each measured filename is matched to the task entity in stimulus filenames; the first match is selected. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L199-L200) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L154-L164) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L175-L178) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L35-L41)

turns.question: What is the functional difference between stimulus_filepath and stimulus.directory?

answers.text: Code: stimulus/directory is used for task-based BIDS discovery. fixed_paths/stimulus_filepath supplies a single stimulus file in non-BIDS mode. The runner selects between these paths using the exact BIDS enable string. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L608-L613) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/bids_handler.py#L175-L191)

turns.question: How do individual and concatenated modes differ in the way they fit runs?

answers.text: Inference from code: Use individual for separate per-file estimates with one stimulus/task, or concatenated to estimate shared parameters from selected BIDS blocks by summing their projection terms. turns.question: How do coarse grid fitting and local refinement differ algorithmically?

answers.text: Inference from code: Grid fitting selects the candidate with the largest projection YᵀS′. Refinement uses neighbouring error/derivative values and coefficient matrices to build a local quadratic and solves pinv(2A)·(-B). This is not an iterative generic optimizer, and this solver does not clamp final parameters to min/max sigma or the grid extent. turns.question: How do coarse grid fitting and local refinement differ algorithmically?

answers.text: Inference from code: Grid fitting selects the candidate with the largest projection YᵀS′. Refinement uses neighbouring error/derivative values and coefficient matrices to build a local quadratic and solves pinv(2A)·(-B). This is not an iterative generic optimizer, and this solver does not clamp final parameters to min/max sigma or the grid extent. answers.text: Code: refine_fitting.enable is parsed as a boolean. True computes model derivatives and local neighbour coefficient matrices, performs a local refinement after the coarse grid choice, and in individual mode rechecks the refined projection against the coarse result. False returns the selected coarse grid parameters. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L115-L121) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L174-L192) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L615-L619) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L336-L362) [source 5](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L275-L299)

Code: refinefit_on_gpu controls whether refinement inputs stay as CuPy arrays. The local solver chooses CuPy or NumPy according to the error-array type. True keeps these fitting terms on GPU; false transfers them to CPU for refinement, while stimulus/model generation and initial projection computation still use GPUs. turns.question: How do coarse grid fitting and local refinement differ algorithmically?

answers.text: Inference from code: Grid fitting selects the candidate with the largest projection YᵀS′. Refinement uses neighbouring error/derivative values and coefficient matrices to build a local quadratic and solves pinv(2A)·(-B). This is not an iterative generic optimizer, and this solver does not clamp final parameters to min/max sigma or the grid extent. turns.question: Can I load only some custom components from a file while generating the remaining components?

answers.text:
Code: search_space/optional_analysis_params has a parent enable flag, filepath attribute, and independent hrf/sigmas/spatial_grid_xy use_from_file flags and key attributes. A component is loaded only when both its child flag and the parent flag are true; the other components are generated from their default settings. turns.question: What units does visual_field_radius use? Separately, what units does visual_field use?

answers.text:
Code: visual_field_radius creates default x/y candidate coordinates spanning ±radius. Setup uses the maximum coordinate of the selected grid as the Gaussian validation radius, and keeps candidate centres satisfying x²+y² < radius², excluding the circle boundary. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L128-L133) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/init_setup.py#L120-L140) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_gaussian_model.py#L69-L72)

Inference from code: stimulus/visual_field is a radius in degrees: the stimulus x and y coordinates each run from -visual_field to +visual_field, giving an axis extent of twice this value. It supplies the coordinate scale for evaluating pRF curves on the resampled stimulus. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/analysis_configs/sample_config.xml#L17-L17) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L107-L110) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_stimulus.py#L37-L42) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/kernels/gaussian_kernel.cu#L49-L60)

turns.question: What would increasing visual_field do? In a separate hypothetical case, what would reducing visual_field_radius do?

answers.text: Inference from code: Increasing visual_field expands the coordinate extent represented by the same stimulus pixels and increases coordinate spacing for fixed width/height. The pRF kernel then compares centres and sigma against this changed coordinate scale; it does not add stimulus pixels or automatically expand the search grid. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_stimulus.py#L37-L42) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/kernels/gaussian_kernel.cu#L49-L60) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L129-L133)

Inference from code: Decreasing a positive default radius contracts candidate-centre positions and grid spacing. It is an extent setting rather than a grid-count setting, and the strict radial mask is still applied. turns.question: Please revise your first explanation: I meant default_hrf.t when I asked what the parameter controls.

answers.text: Code: default_hrf/t is a pair (start,stop), parsed as floats and unpacked into arange(start,stop,TR). stop is excluded. The values share the time unit of TR (seconds in the header-fallback log); this is an interval, not a single scalar duration. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88)

turns.question: In my separate question about units, I meant default_hrf.t rather than TR. Could you correct that answer?

answers.text: Code: default_hrf/t is a pair (start,stop), parsed as floats and unpacked into arange(start,stop,TR). stop is excluded. The values share the time unit of TR (seconds in the header-fallback log); this is an interval, not a single scalar duration. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88)
answers.display_text:
Code: default_hrf/t is a pair (start,stop), parsed as floats and unpacked into arange(start,stop,TR). stop is excluded. The values share the time unit of TR (seconds in the header-fallback log); this is an interval, not a single scalar duration. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88)

Precision qualification: the preceding endpoint statement describes the intended half-open interval, not a floating-point guarantee. NumPy documents that rounding with a non-integer step can include stop, and floating-point result sizing can put the last value beyond stop. [NumPy 1.22 arange documentation](https://numpy.org/doc/1.22/reference/generated/numpy.arange.html)

turns.question: How is TR handled if it is present in the configuration but its value is empty?

answers.text: Inference from code: An empty TR attribute or a value such as auto parses to None, then HRF generation reads stimulus.Header['pixdim'][4]. The parser accepts unsigned decimal strings as floats, but treats scientific notation, negatives and other non-digit forms as None. Omitting the TR attribute entirely can instead fail on dictionary lookup; this is not a measured-fMRI-header fallback. turns.question: What shape does a loaded HRF array require?

answers.text: Inference from code: Supply a one-dimensional numeric HRF sample array. answers.text:
Inference from code: Supply a one-dimensional numeric vector of sigma values. It is returned unchanged by the HDF5 reader and used as an extra dimension: the grid code takes its length and assigns individual entries as scalar sigma coordinates. There is no flattening, sorting, or positivity validation in this load path. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/utils/gem_h5_file_handler.py#L18-L24) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L136-L146) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/space/PRFSpace.py#L354-L374) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_gaussian_model.py#L69-L72)

Inference from code: For refinement, sigma neighbours are chosen by adjacent positions in the supplied sigma vector (index-1 through index+1 around the nearest value). The loader does not sort that vector. Therefore array ordering, especially for irregular custom sigmas, affects local-neighbour geometry and should reflect the intended neighbouring sizes. lineage.split_lock: dev

turns.question: With optional_params.enable disabled, is optional_params.filepath used? Under that same disabled parent, is hrf.use_from_file used?

answers.text: Code: With the parent enable flag false, these component-loading branches do not open the custom file or use the keys, regardless of child use_from_file values. The configuration loader still parses the flag/path/key attributes and default settings. Code: hrf.use_from_file takes effect only together with optional_analysis_params.enable. When both are true, the configured file/key array is loaded; otherwise this component follows its generated/default branch. author: dev_author

review.interpretation: Actual batch count exceeds measured signal count; distinguish individual/concatenated behavior.

turns.question: My batches setting is larger than the number of measured voxel or vertex signals. What behavior follows from that relation?

answers.text:
Code: measured_data/batches is converted to int and controls the number of measured signals handled per batch, not timepoints or model-grid density. Individual batch_size is max(1, int(number_of_signals/batches)); the final batch may be smaller. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L307-L324)

Inference from code: Concatenated mode instead uses int(number_of_signals/batches) without max(1, ...). If batches exceeds the number of signals, the resulting zero step in range fails. Zero batches also causes division by zero; a positive usable count is required. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L479-L492)

turns.question: Suppose a GPU out-of-memory error occurs while refinefit_on_gpu is disabled. What behavior is documented in that case, including any retry behavior?

answers.text:
Inference from code: The active refinement solver directly allocates/operates on its chosen backend and does not catch GPU out-of-memory errors or automatically retry refinement on CPU. More measured-data batches can reduce per-batch fitting arrays; selecting CPU refinement moves those computations, but other GPU allocations remain. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/fitting/hpc_refine_fit.py#L66-L105) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/fitting/hpc_refine_fit.py#L110-L146) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/fitting/hpc_grid_fit.py#L47-L58) [source 4](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L319-L345)

answers.text:
Code: measured_data/batches is converted to int and controls the number of measured signals handled per batch, not timepoints or model-grid density. Individual batch_size is max(1, int(number_of_signals/batches)); the final batch may be smaller. Inference from code: Concatenated mode instead uses int(number_of_signals/batches) without max(1, ...). If batches exceeds the number of signals, the resulting zero step in range fails. Zero batches also causes division by zero; a positive usable count is required. turns.question: Is num_frames_downsampled used when high_temporal_resolution.enable is disabled?

turns.question: Suppose num_frames_downsampled does not match the measured fMRI timecourse length. What would happen?

answers.text:
Inference from code: Set the target count from the measured timecourse length that should be modelled after downsampling. The loader treats the last measured image dimension as time and individual fitting enforces equality; it does not estimate an ideal target count. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/data/observed_data.py#L43-L57) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L314-L317) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/signal_synthesizer.py#L219-L229)

Inference from code: Individual fitting requires the loaded measured-data time length to equal stimulus.NumFrames, or NumFramesDownsampled when high temporal resolution is enabled. A mismatch logs an error and exits with status 1; correct the file/selected mode and their actual time lengths. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L307-L317) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_stimulus.py#L78-L92)

turns.question: The parameters for that units question are TR and default_hrf.t, in that order.

answers.text: Code: default_hrf/TR is the sampling step of the generated HRF time vector: arange(t_start,t_stop,TR). It does not resample the measured fMRI data. If its parsed value is None, the step comes from the stimulus header pixdim[4], which the code reports in seconds. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162)

Code: default_hrf/t is a pair (start,stop), parsed as floats and unpacked into arange(start,stop,TR). stop is excluded. The values share the time unit of TR (seconds in the header-fallback log); this is an interval, not a single scalar duration. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88)

answers.text: Code: binarization enable is active only for the exact string "True". Code: high_temporal_resolution.enable is parsed case-insensitively. When true, model signals are computed from the stimulus frames after HRF convolution and then sampled to num_frames_downsampled with an index shift controlled by slice_time_ref. answers.text: Inference from code: Choose a start/stop interval that contains the HRF kernel you intend to use at the chosen sampling step. t and TR jointly define the samples; the code does not derive a subject-specific ideal interval or require stop to be an integer multiple of TR. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/signals/hrf_generator.py#L47-L64)
answers.display_text:
Code: default_hrf.t is parsed as a pair (start, stop), and the generated-HRF path calls np.arange(start, stop, TR). Code: default_hrf.t is parsed as a pair (start, stop), and the generated-HRF path calls np.arange(start, stop, TR). TR is the sampling step; with positive TR, the intended interval is [start, stop), excluding stop. Floating-point rounding can nevertheless include stop or put the last sample beyond it, so endpoint exclusion is not an unconditional numerical guarantee. [tuple parser](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/configs/config_manager.py#L153-L162) [sample construction](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L69-L88) [NumPy 1.22 arange documentation](https://numpy.org/doc/1.22/reference/generated/numpy.arange.html)

answers.text: Inference from code: Choose a start/stop interval that contains the HRF kernel you intend to use at the chosen sampling step. t and TR jointly define the samples; the code does not derive a subject-specific ideal interval or require stop to be an integer multiple of TR. answers.display_text:
Code: default_hrf.t is parsed as a pair (start, stop), and the generated-HRF path calls np.arange(start, stop, TR). answers.text:
Code: visual_field_radius creates default x/y candidate coordinates spanning ±radius. Setup uses the maximum coordinate of the selected grid as the Gaussian validation radius, and keeps candidate centres satisfying x²+y² < radius², excluding the circle boundary. [source 1](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/run/run_gem_prf_analysis.py#L128-L133) [source 2](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/init_setup.py#L120-L140) [source 3](https://github.com/siddmittal/GEMpRF/blob/c35f9fddbca98df24af24ee478b7f843b02a3f81/gem/model/prf_gaussian_model.py#L69-L72)

Inference from code: stimulus/visual_field is a radius in degrees: the stimulus x and y coordinates each run from -visual_field to +visual_field, giving an axis extent of twice this value. It supplies the coordinate scale for evaluating pRF curves on the resampled stimulus.
